short: Anima illustration: base first, then the Tile way

title.zh: Anima 插画·底图与 Tile 细化
title.en: Anima illustration: base and Tile detail

about.zh: Anima 插画分两步时怎么判断：先出底图给你看，再用“Anima Tile 放大细化”这块做法细化；你存过这条路线的工作流或搭配就直接用；你没选的画风、LoRA、画师词不加。具体数值在做法和你自己的搭配里，这里不写。
about.en: How to judge an Anima illustration in two passes: show the base first, then refine it with the "Anima Tile detail upscale" way; a workflow or combo you saved for this route is used as it is; no style, LoRA or artist you did not pick. The values live in the way and in your own combos, not here.

text: Use for an Anima illustration the user wants refined in two passes, not as a default for other models or styles. Preserve the user's text, requested character and pose; add a style, artist or LoRA only when the user picked it (a combo or saved prompt of theirs).

If the user saved this route as a workflow (list_workflows lists it with its plans) or a combo (list_combos), use it: run_workflow(workflow="name" or "name / plan") with their subject and seed is the daily run. Its models and values are theirs: do not change them; pick another plan instead when the user wants the other route.

Run the base first and show it; when the user wants to choose, let them pick it before the second pass. Then add_nodes(block="upscale_anima_tile") on the Anima canvas: the way carries the tested second-pass values and checks the model family and the Tile weight. Report a missing node or model; never swap in a look-alike.

What to expect: a high-denoise second pass without Tile tends to change the pose and ornaments; with Tile the composition holds better, but faces, hands and small details are still redrawn. Keep the base, compare, and lower the denoise when keeping more matters to the user.

Changing models between the passes: only within one family sharing the text encoder and VAE; otherwise say it is untried. These findings come from a few single-seed comparisons: say what ran and what changed, and do not promise a reproduction or repaired hands.
